label: Completeness
description: Whether quantum mechanics says everything there is to say about a single system.

label: Determinism
description: Whether the present state fixes the future uniquely.

label: Probability
description: Whether the probabilities of the theory are fundamental or a cover for ignorance.

label: Causality
description: The causal law and its fate in atomic processes.

label: The wave function
description: What ψ is: a real wave, a probability, a statement of knowledge.

label: Measurement
description: What happens when an atomic system meets an instrument.

label: Realism
description: Whether systems have properties independent of observation.

label: Further determining quantities
description: Whether additional quantities could fix individual outcomes (later called hidden variables).

label: Anschaulichkeit
description: Whether physics must give pictures in space and time.

label: Waves and quanta
description: The dual behaviour of light and matter.

label: Quantum jumps
description: Discontinuous transitions between stationary states.

label: Local action
description: Whether influences can act instantaneously at a distance.

label: Complementarity
description: Bohr's framework of mutually exclusive but jointly necessary descriptions.

label: Observables
description: Whether theory should speak only of observable quantities.

label: Formalism
description: The mathematical structure: matrices, waves, transformation theory.

label: Experiment
description: What the laboratory had shown by 1927.

label: Radiation
description: Emission, absorption and the quantum of action.

label: Classical limit
description: How classical mechanics re-emerges.

label: Cosmology
description: The universe as a whole.

label: Gravitation
description: General relativity and its consequences.

label: Fields and particles
description: Relativistic quantum theory of fields.

label: Computation
description: Computing and information.
